title: Quickstep handoff playlog
body:
Quickstep handoff playlog

Context: quick, informal handoff after a short but noisy afternoon spike. This document is a scratchpad for the incoming engineer — not polished, will iterate into the official runbook once root cause confirmed.

Summary (what happened):
- 2025-11-02 16:12 UTC: sudden latency spike for /v1/generate on hosted-api (p95 jumped from 180ms to ~2.4s).
- Error rates increased for model-allocs on us-east-1 dedicated pool (504s and websocket disconnects).
- Autoscaler triggered two additional nodes but they joined slowly; fallback routing masked some traffic.
- Mitigations applied: temporary rate-limit increase for premium-traffic disabled; rolled back recent kernel patch on serving-runtime-canary (PR #987).

Immediate status:
- Alerting: noisy alerts throttled, currently suppressed for the duration of triage.
- Services: hosting-api frontends healthy; pool us-east-1-dedicated showing degraded but stable (some request queueing).
- Owner: Aisha (leaving), handoff to Marcus.

Things I did (quick chronological log):
- 16:15: checked Grafana: dashboard "API Latency /v1/generate" and "Dedicated pool - us-east-1".
- 16:18: looked at recent deploys (git tag v2025.11.02-runtime-canary). Noted PR 987 applied at 16:05.
- 16:22: kicked canary rollback for serving-runtime-canary -> reverted to v2025.10.28.
- 16:30: scaled up dedicated pool manually (added 2x g5.2xlarge equiv). Autoscaler later added one more.
- 16:42: monitored connection churn; started temporarily routing low-priority traffic to fallback-model-legacy.

Quick ops checklist for the incoming shift (do these first):
1) Confirm alerts in PagerDuty: check recent incident INF-4321 and add notes.
2) Verify rollback status: kubectl get pods -n serving | grep canary -> ensure all pods show v2025.10.28 image.
3) Check node-level metrics for us-east-1-dedicated (GPU memory, OOM events). Grafana dashboards: "Dedicated GPU Utilization" and "Serving Runtime - KV cache pressure".
4) Watch for queue length on request-queue-1: prometheus query: sum(rate(request_queue_depth[1m])) by (pool).
5) If queue depth > 500 sustained for 5+ min, consider: - throttle non-production tenants - bump dedicated pool by 1 node - enable fallback routing for embeddings only.

Useful commands (copy/paste):
- kubectl -n serving rollout status deploy/serving-runtime-canary
- kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide | grep serving-runtime
- kubectl -n infra logs deployment/autoscaler --since=30m
- curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gptx-8b"}'
- prometheus: sum(rate(requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[1m]))

Notes on what to watch (sensors):
- p95 latency for /v1/generate (Grafana panel)
- model-allocation error rate (logs): search logs in Grafana/Elk for "allocation failed" and "kv_cache_miss_spike"
- websocket disconnects for streaming requests (metric: stream_disconnects_total)
- node GPU mem pressure & driver restarts (metric: nvidia_driver_restarts)

Temporary mitigations applied (do not remove without approval):
- rollback of runtime canary (PR 987) - timestamped in deploy history.
- suppressed alerting rule: SRE-Latency-Spike for INF-4321 (note: suppression will auto-clear in 2h).
- routing rule: low_priority -> fallback-model-legacy; tag: routing-temp-2025-11-02.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Did kernel-level change in PR 987 cause KV cache eviction storms? Need to compare metrics pre/post (16:00).
- Why autoscaler latency was slow to provision pods? Look at cloud provider quota events and cluster-autoscaler logs.
- Is there any correlation with nightly backup jobs (db-snap) that started at 15:50? Check infra job schedule.

Follow-ups to action (assign / due):
- Diego: collect detailed pod logs for serving-runtime-canary between 15:45-16:30 (ticket INF-4321) — due EOD 2025-11-03.
- Marcus (you): verify autoscaler cloud quota and file support ticket with cloud if capacity provisioning > 5min — priority high.
- Me (Aisha): write root-cause hypothesis draft and push to Confluence under "Incident INF-4321".

Escalation contacts (fast):
- Marcus Lee (on-call lead): +1-415-555-0123 (slack: @marcus)
- Diego Alvarez (infra): +1-650-555-0199 (slack: @diego)
- PagerDuty: incident INF-4321 -> follow the usual SRE playbook

Notes to self (informal):
- remember to add a small note about the fallback-model latency differences; downstream UX may see token dropouts.
- when converting to real runbook, add explicit thresholds for queue depth and per-pool scaling steps.

Small checklist before I sign off: [x] add this doc to the INF ticket [x] notify #oncall in Slack with short summary [ ] confirm autoscaler logs uploaded to ticket [ ] coordinate next-day deep-dive with runtime team

Anything else:
- If you see renewed websocket flaps, immediately disable streaming for non-premium routes (config: routing/streaming-enabled=false) then notify customers.
- Keep an eye on billing alerts if we keep scaling up for longer than 3 hours (cost center: dedicated-us-east-1).

End of quickstep playlog. Reilly: if you pick this up later, append notes and move tasks into INF-4321.

-- Aisha
